documents.title: New year refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy requests new 90-day prescriptions under his new plan year: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succinate 50, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30. Sent, 90 days x 3. Imatinib and capecitabine come from the oncology specialty pharmacy, not us.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. On capecitabine cycle 10ish, imatinib ongoing. December CT showed the liver spots shrinking, BCR-ABL in major molecular response - he's encouraged. Back to jogging short distances. Tremor same.
Home BP 140s/90. No chest pain, palpitations rare.
Exam: BP above goal. Lungs clear, heart regular, no edema.
A/P: HTN above goal on lisinopril/HCTZ - continue, BMP today. Cancer care per oncology. CAD/pAF stable. RTC 6 mo for physical.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT CHEST, ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST. Comparison 12/12/2022. Liver: segment 7 lesion 1.1 cm, unchanged; segment 4a and 3 lesions faint and unchanged. No new liver lesion. Anastomosis unremarkable. No adenopathy, ascites or peritoneal nodularity. Chest: lungs clear.
reports.conclusion: Stable hepatic metastases. No new disease.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology/hematology clinic. Date of service: 04/14/2023.

Stage IV colon adenocarcinoma on capecitabine 1500 mg twice daily days 1-14 q21d. Feels well, working. CT 04/10/2023: stable liver disease, no new sites. CBC/CMP normal. CML on imatinib, last BCR-ABL1 0.07%.
Plan: continue both agents. Next CT in 4 months.

Outside oncology

documents.title: My brother
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know - after everything with me my older brother finally got a colonoscopy and they found colon cancer too. He's 61. He's having surgery next month. Does this change anything for me?

documents.title: RE: My brother
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm sorry to hear that, Brian. It doesn't change your own treatment, but it matters for the family history in your chart and for your relatives' screening. Our nurse will call to update your record.

documents.title: Family history update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with pt. Older brother (61) diagnosed with colon cancer in May after a screening colonoscopy. Family history updated. Reviewed that this does not change his own care. Nothing else needed.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT CHEST, ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST. Comparison 04/10/2023. Hepatic lesions unchanged in size and number, largest 1.1 cm in segment 7. No new lesion. No local recurrence at the anastomosis. No adenopathy. Lungs clear.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
60 yo, yearly exam. One year into capecitabine with stable liver disease on the last two CTs; CML in major molecular response on imatinib. Feels pretty normal day to day. Jogging 2 miles a few times a week. Brother had his surgery in July and is recovering.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succ 50, ISMN 30, ASA 81, imatinib 400, capecitabine 1500 BID d1-14 q21. NKDA.
Family hx: father HTN/tremor/MI at 62; mother DM2; brother colon ca at 61.
Exam: BP above goal. Well. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, healed incisions. No edema. Postural tremor both hands, mild.
A/P
- HTN above goal, unchanged regimen. BMP.
- Colon ca stage IV, CML: per oncology/hematology.
- CAD, pAF, essential tremor: stable.
- ED: hasn't pursued urology's options, no new concerns.
- Flu + updated COVID today. Lipids, A1c. PHQ-2 0.
RTC 4-5 mo.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, office visit 10/17/2023.

Mr. Goodwin remains on capecitabine and imatinib without cardiac events. Exertional tightness rare and unchanged; he jogs. Occasional palpitations lasting minutes. BP 142/88, HR 64. ECG: sinus rhythm, normal QRS, no ischemic change.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, aspirin 81 mg, imatinib 400 mg, capecitabine. NKDA.

Impression: stable angina; paroxysmal AF, infrequent. No change. One year, sooner if palpitations increase.

Outside cardiology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, 61. Two years of stable liver disease on capecitabine, CML in deep molecular response. Palpitation spells more frequent over the summer - several a week, up to half an hour. Seeing cardiology next month and will raise it.
Meds unchanged. NKDA.
Exam: BP above goal. HR regular at rest today. Lungs clear. No edema. Tremor unchanged.
A/P
- Palpitations, known pAF: more frequent; cardiology 11/5. If a long episode or chest pain, go to the ED.
- HTN above goal, unchanged.
- Oncology issues per their team.
- Flu, updated COVID. Lipids, A1c, BMP.
RTC 4 mo.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

reports.text: 12-lead ECG (outside cardiology). Atrial fibrillation, ventricular rate 92. QRS 94 ms, normal axis. No acute ST change.
reports.conclusion: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular rate, normal QRS duration.

documents.title: Cardiology visit letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, office visit 11/05/2024.

Mr. Goodwin reports more frequent palpitation spells since summer, several a week, some lasting up to 30 minutes. He was in atrial fibrillation at today's visit, rate 92, normal QRS duration. BP 140/86.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, aspirin 81 mg, imatinib 400 mg, capecitabine. NKDA.

Impression: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, more symptomatic.
Plan: start flecainide 100 mg twice daily for rhythm control; continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg. Call with any fainting or prolonged palpitations. Return in 6 months.

Outside cardiology
